issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (with methods like add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock), but the template repository provides an 'Inventory' class that implements these methods while Stock.java is empty. The solution also uses Inventory as the shared stock type in SealSaloon. This name/type mismatch and the presence of an empty Stock.java file is a structural inconsistency that could confuse students about which class they should use or modify (Stock vs Inventory).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent: either (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to 'Inventory' instead of 'Stock', or (B) provide a concrete 'Stock' implementation in the template (move/duplicate the Inventory implementation into Stock.java and update references) and remove or deprecate Inventory. Ensure SealSaloon and all documentation/tests refer to the same class name so students know which class to use/modify.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock', but the provided codebase (both template and solution) implements and uses a class named 'Inventory' for the same conceptual entity. This mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) can confuse students when mapping the requirements/diagram to the starter code and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across all artifacts. Either rename the code-side class and files from Inventory to Stock (and update all references in SealSaloon and other files), or update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Also remove or populate the empty Stock.java file so students are not misled by an unused/empty class file.
